fields.markdown:
**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 325 **Complexity** Complex The floor of this circular room pivots and shifts awkwardly when weight is placed upon its surface, pitching those who attempt to walk on it off their feet and potentially into one of two deep spiked pits. --- **Stealth** DC 37 (expert) **Disable** Thievery DC 37 (expert) to wedge scraps of material into the edges of the room to hamper the floor's tilt (requires 4 successes). **Tilt and Roll** **Trigger** A creature or object of at least 3 bulk moves onto the floor; the trap can use this reaction multiple times in a round, but only once per triggering creature or object; **Effect** The floor pitches and rolls. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The character can move across the room normally this turn, without having to attempt Acrobatics checks, but treats the unstable floor as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453).
**Success** The character treats the ground in this room as difficult terrain, but each time they move they must succeed at a DC 30 Acrobatics check or they fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) at the start of their turn. A character who falls prone must succeed at a DC 33 Reflex save or fall into one of the two spiked pits to the north or south of the room (see Failure).
**Failure** As success but the character automatically falls prone and must succeed at a DC 33 Reflex save to avoid being pitched into one of the two spiked pits to the north or south of the room. A character who is pitched into a pit can attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) to avoid falling. The DC to Grab an Edge or [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) a pit's walls is 33.
A character who falls into one of the pits plunges 50 feet onto a bed of spikes, taking 25 points of bludgeoning damage and 2d6 piercing damage (DC 33 basic Reflex save).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the character automatically rolls into one of the two pits. --- **Routine** (1 action) On its initiative each turn, the floor tilts randomly, forcing all characters standing on the floor of the room to attempt a DC 33 Reflex save to avoid being pitched into one of the two pits.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #188: They Watched the Stars](/Sources.aspx?ID=194) pg. 63 **Complexity** Complex An incorporeal Sarkorian deity manifests before the party and challenges their resolve. Only aspirants whose motives are pure and whose hearts are in tune with the natural world can hope to overcome this “test of the god caller.” --- **Stealth** +12 (expert) **Disable** Three DC 27 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) or [Occultism](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) (trained) checks can disable the haunt **Manifest** **Trigger** Sakuachi makes an offering at the well shrine; **Effect** The Sarkorian deity inhabiting the well surges to life, manifesting as a large, ghostly beast surrounded by throngs of smaller animals. The rush of spiritual energy washes over everyone in the well, dealing 8d6 force damage (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). --- **Routine** (3 actions) The Sarkorian divinity commands a swarm of ghostly animals to overwhelm creatures in a 10-foot burst in the well. The haunt can select up to three different points to target, spending 1 action per burst. Creatures in an affected take 4d6 force damage and must attempt a DC 25 Will save. The haunt loses 1 action for each successful check to disable the haunt.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes half damage.
**Failure** The target takes full damage and is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the beginning of the haunt's next turn.
**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage, is flat-footed until the beginning of the haunt's next turn, and is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round. --- **Reset** 8 hours

<title level="1" right="Hazard 12" pfs="">[Thalassophobic Pool](/Hazards.aspx?ID=195)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 212

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The pool sucks in creatures that fall into it, making them sink into its endless depths.

---

**Stealth**
DC 25 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 32 (master) [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) to quell the fear and calm the pool or DC 35 [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) to give the pool something worse to fear; three successes required.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Downpour** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature falls into the pool; **Effect** More water pours forth from the chalice. Creatures in the pool become clumsy 1, and they can't decrease their clumsy condition so long as they remain in the pool. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) Water from the chalice increases the depth of the water by 10 feet for each action. Each time this happens, creatures in the pool are pushed 10 feet down and take 1d6 bludgeoning damage. As the pool has no bottom, creatures in it can fall down indefinitely; they must [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) up to avoid drowning, but the water is especially choppy, so the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) DC is 25. The pool never overflows. Each successful check to Disable reduces the pool's actions by 1, and once the pool is completely Disabled, the water becomes still and the Athletics DC to Swim becomes 10.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets once there are no moving creatures in it.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 11 **Complexity** Complex The Avalanche rests as a gem on a stone pedestal, continually unleashing natural disasters in the nearby area. --- **Stealth** +37 (master) **Disable** Two DC 41 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) or DC 43 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to approach the pedestal, resisting the quaking earth and other hazards and eventually holding strong enough to take the gem from the pedestal; a creature who can approach the pedestal without touching the ground, such as by jumping or flying, can simply snatch the gem and end the Avalanche's assault **Shuddering Boom** ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93)) **Trigger** The PCs reach the area depicted on the Trial of the Avalanche map; **Effect** The Avalanche shudders, causing a thunderous boom to fill the area. All creatures without the [Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) trait in the area must succeed at a DC 39 Fortitude save or become [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) (stunned 3 on a critical failure). The Avalanche then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) The Avalanche releases its fury at a point within 120 feet, affecting all creatures within its area. Each creature must attempt a DC 41 Reflex save to hold their ground or avoid the incoming danger. The amount and type of damage dealt are based on the nature of the natural disaster the Avalanche unleashes, and certain types of disasters impose additional effects. The Avalanche can't unleash the same type of disaster twice in a row. The [sturzstromer](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1100) is immune to these effects.
  • **Earthquake** The ground in a 20-foot burst violently shakes and launches rubble in the area, dealing 3d12+20 bludgeoning damage. On a failure, the creature also [stumbles back 5 feet](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), away from the Avalanche. On a critical failure, the creature stumbles back 10 feet and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).
  • **Fire Rain** A hail of burning rock rains down in a 20-foot-burst, dealing 3d12+20 fire damage. Creatures that fail their save catch on fire and take 2d6 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) (double on a critical failure).
  • **Landslide** A mass of rubble falls in a 10-foot-burst, dealing 9d8 bludgeoning damage. Creatures that critically fail their save become trapped under this rubble as if it were an [avalanche](/Rules.aspx?ID=646), except a creature can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) from beneath the rubble (DC 40).
  • **Lava Channel** A burst of molten rock violently spews forth in a 30-foot-long and 10-foot-wide line, dealing 9d8 fire damage. Creatures that fail their Reflex save are swept 15 feet away by the lava (30 feet on a critical failure). The lava cools almost instantly, allowing creatures to walk over its path immediately after resolving the effects of the disaster.
  • **Powerful Winds** A massive burst of wind travels in a 60-foot line, kicking up dust and dealing 3d12+20 slashing damage. Creatures that fail their Reflex save become [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round and also fall prone on a critical failure.
    **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
    **Success** The creature takes half damage.
    **Failure** The creature takes full damage.
    **Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [The Private Halls](/Sources.aspx?ID=363) pg. 176 **Complexity** Complex The dreamwell plant shudders and pulses, emitting more potent odors before it bursts into swarms of ravenous ghostly spiders. --- **Stealth** +23 (master) **Disable** DC 33 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) (master) to use the dreamwell plant’s own blooms to soothe the ghostly spiders or DC 36 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (trained) to exorcise the ghostly spiders; three successes are required to disable the haunt completely **AC** 31, **Fort** +24, **Ref** +18 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 80 (BT 40) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Weaknesses** axes 10, fire 10, vitality 10 **Resistances** bludgeoning 10, piercing 10 **Dreamtime Bloom** (incapacitation, mental, sleep) **Trigger** A Small or larger living creature spends more than a minute in the room, or anyone attempts to move or damage the plant; **Effect** The dreamwell plant’s flowers bloom and fill the air in area **F14** with soporific scents. All creatures in the room must attempt a DC 30 Will save with the following effects; the haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The character is unaffected.
**Success** The character takes a –1 status penalty to their initiative roll at the start of the following round.
**Failure** As success, but the character is also [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 from sudden tiredness. The affected character can attempt a new DC 30 Will save at the end of a round to recover from this condition; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The character falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95). If it’s still unconscious (and alive) after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically. --- **Routine** (2 actions) An immense swarm of thumb-sized spiders boil out of the plant’s planter box and its bulbous trunk, filling the air with the nauseating sound of tens of thousands of tiny clawed feet scuttling everywhere. The haunt uses its first action to spray webbing through the area so that every creature in the room must succeed at a DC 30 Reflex save to avoid taking a –5-foot status penalty to their Speed. These penalties stack with multiple failed Reflex saves, and a character whose penalties reduce their Speed to 0 becomes [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) (Escape DC 30). On its second action, the phantasmal spiders begin to bite and gnaw at living flesh with fangs that are suddenly both very real and very toxic. Every creature in the room takes 2d10 piercing and 2d10 poison damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates at the end of any round in which there are no Small or larger living creatures in the room, then resets automatically.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 9" pfs="">[The Bastard's Portrait](/Hazards.aspx?ID=762)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=622" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Reception Halls](/Sources.aspx?ID=361) pg. 109

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A mysterious portrait lies face down on the floor.

---

**Stealth**
+20 (master)

**Disable**
DC 31 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to carefully dismantle the portrait without jostling it enough to trigger it or DC 33 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (expert) to exorcise the haunt; 3 successes are required to disable it.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**You Will Know My Name!** <actions string="Reaction" /> (emotion, fear, mental, occult, visual) **Trigger** A creature attempts to move the portrait; **Effect** Once someone flips the portrait over, they see a headless man portrayed in fine clothing, only to have the name “VELICARN” appear across the portrait in the form of bloody letters that run from the headless man’s raw stump. If the triggering creature didn’t attempt to look at the portrait, the painting wrenches and twists to present itself to the target, who must succeed at a DC 28 Will save to avoid becoming [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). A moment later, a trio of shadowy forms that drip and splatter blood surge out from the portrait, leaving it a blank canvas. These shapes appear vaguely as headless humanoids made of red smoke and leave bloodstains wherever they touch, but they’re otherwise treated as typical wraiths. The wraiths roll initiative and remain for 1 minute, after which they vanish, and the portrait becomes a blank but bloodstained canvas. The wraiths also vanish if someone disables the haunt before the duration expires.

fields.disable: This is the end of days. The Doom of Azlant cannot be disabled or averted in any way.
fields.markdown:
**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 126 **Complexity** Complex Fiery rocks from space crash through the skylight ceiling of the Azlanti throne room, showering those below in ceaseless cascades of fire and broken glass. --- **Stealth** +0 (untrained) **Disable** This is the end of days. The Doom of Azlant cannot be disabled or averted in any way. **Falling Star** **Trigger** Delharia’s turn begins on round 6 of the battle; **Effect** Disaster strikes! A flaming meteorite blasts through the chamber’s ceiling in a cacophony of shattered glass and explosive force and slams directly into the spot along the western wall where Delharia and her protectors make their last stand (room segment 3). The resulting blast completely annihilates Delharia, her protectors, and the palace guards attacking her. The pillar in this section against the wall topples to the ground with a huge crash, sizzling with a loud hiss when the waters within splash against the sudden conflagration. If any PCs are in room segment 3, they are affected by the Falling Star as well, as detailed in the routine below. The Doom of Azlant doesn’t roll initiative; its routine plays out at the end of each following round, starting with round 7. --- **Routine** (1 action) At the end of each round, starting on round 7, roll 1d8 to determine which section of the throne room of Azlant is struck by another Falling Star, rerolling results that indicate sections that have already been destroyed. The Falling Star destroys that section of the room, as well as any undestroyed pillars potentially containing veiled masters. Non-statted NPCs in that room section are killed instantly, consumed by otherworldly flame and crushed by flying debris. All PCs, palace guards, and vidileths not currently in a pillar who are in the room segment take 2d6+4 bludgeoning damage and 2d6 fire damage (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). A critical failure also knocks the creature [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

Destroyed room sections function as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366), but also pose additional dangers. The first time during a character’s turn that they take any action with the [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) trait that takes place wholly or partially in a destroyed room segment, roll 1d6 and consult the following additional dangers to see what that character must endure as a result of their movement.
**1–2 Desperate Courtier** Seemingly from out of nowhere, one of the servants or lesser nobles [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) in terror leaps upon the character, desperately clinging to their clothing and limbs and making movement more difficult. The character can avoid the courtier with a successful DC 24 Reflex save, otherwise the character takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to their Speed until they can [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 20) from the desperate courtier’s clutches. Vidileths ignore this result, as no courtier is desperate enough to cling to one of these monsters!
**3–4 Hail of Meteorites** A bright red barrage of scalding space debris pummels the character for 1d6+4 bludgeoning damage and 1d6 fire damage, with additional effects determined by a DC 24 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes full damage, is knocked prone, and takes an additional 2d6 [persistent fire damage.](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29)
**5–6 Shearing Glass** A razor-sharp sheet of jagged green glass tumbles down from the ceiling and threatens to bisect the victim. The creature takes 2d6 slashing damage, with additional effects determined by a DC 24 Reflex save. If the slashing damage from the glass reduces a creature to 0 HP, a pane of glass shears straight through the victim's neck, slicing off their head and killing them instantly. **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and 1d6 persistent bleed damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and 2d6 persistent bleed damage.

+0 (trained)

reduce the Eclipse to 0 HP, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (10th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 39) to counteract the Eclipse (once it's in range)

32

124 (BT 64)

critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

**Herald the End** <actions string="" /> **Trigger** The PCs arrive at the island; **Effect** A fiery point of light appears in the sky at the  center of the Eclipse, swiftly growing in size as it becomes apparent that a meteor is hurtling toward the island. The Eclipse rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) The Eclipse heals 50 points of damage, retreats upward from PCs if any have approached (as determined by its Distance Score), then unleashes a meteor down on the island below. The meteor explodes upon striking the island, creating a 30-foot radius burst that inflicts 8d6 fire and 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to all creatures caught in the blast. The eclipse targets these strikes to catch as many PCs in the blast as it can each time—while it doesn't seek to damage a [bul-gae](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1411), it won't worry about catching one or both in the area of effect if that spot is the most advantageous to striking the most possible PCs.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [The Enmity Cycle](/Sources.aspx?ID=200) pg. 51 **Complexity** Complex Discordant music, dance, and poetry combine to build a deep suspicion and distrust of strangers. --- **Stealth** +16 (expert) or [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) **Disable** [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) DC 26 to counteract the performance or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) DC 27 to disrupt the spiritual energy. Three total successes are needed to disable the trap. **Discordant Performance** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)); **Trigger** [Zridi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2542) spends an action to activate _The Enmity Cycle_ while in area **F2**; **Effect** All creatures other than Zridi in **F2** take 2d8+9 mental damage (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) The performance continues to sow seeds of enmity, discord, and distrust on those in its area. All creatures in attendance other than Zridi must attempt a DC 25 Will save.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected and is immune to the effects for 1 day.
**Success** The target is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) for 2 rounds.
**Failure** The target is frightened 2 for 1 minute and is certain the source of this fear is their fellow citizens, especially those from places other than their hometown. For 1 week the target suffers a –2 penalty to all [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) skill checks against people from other Thuvian cities and regains the frightened 2 condition whenever they are in one of those cities.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target becomes a carrier for _The Enmity Cycle_ for the next week. The target is compelled to travel to a city other than where they were exposed and recite as many lines from the anbarit as they can recall. Those who hear or witness the performance are treated as if they had attended a performance of _The Enmity Cycle_, but the Will save DC is 23. --- **Reset** A new production of _The Enmity Cycle_ must be arranged; this process usually takes at least 1 week.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 6" pfs="">[The Last Crucible](/Hazards.aspx?ID=258)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 100

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Magically hardened sheets of obsidian drop down over the room's exits while the machinery within taps into wells of magma to begin spewing lava—and monsters—into the maze.

---

**Stealth**
+15 (expert)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 28 (expert) to disable the main pressure plate at area H4a and deactivate the trap entirely (this causes the obsidian walls to retract up into the ceiling as well), Thievery DC 25 (trained) to disable one of the three lava spouts, or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) DC 28 (trained) to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) a fallen obsidian wall

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 22, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +11

**Obsidian Wall Hardness**
15

**Obsidian Wall HP**
58 (BT 29) to smash a 5-foot-square hole in the wall; **Spout Hardness** 13; **Spout HP** 20 (BT 10)

**Immunities**
critical hits, fire, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Drop the Wall** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** Four or more Small or larger creatures walk onto the pressure plate at area H4a; **Effect** A magically hardened sheet of obsidian drops down like a portcullis in the western and northern entrances to this room that lead to areas H3 and H5, respectively. Any creatures standing in one of these squares takes 4d6+4 bludgeoning damage from the falling wall (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) and then decides what side of the wall they want to be on. At the same moment, four [thoqquas](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2185) that have spent centuries in hibernation awaken and emerge from vents into area H4b. The trap then rolls initiative, as do the thoqquas.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The trap loses 1 action per disabled spout each turn. On each action, a different spout located at one of the three areas marked H4c spews a gout of lava at the closest non-thoqqua target in its line of sight; these spouts use magical sensors that have [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) and a Perception DC of 25. Originally, agents of the abbot would come through here after the trap was triggered, deactivate it, and clean out the hardened blobs of lava and dead bodies that remained, but the amount of time it would take for this trap to clog tunnels with cooled lava makes tracking that slow accretion over the course of this adventure unnecessary.

 **Ranged** <actions string="Single Action" /> lava gout +17 (fire), **Damage** 4d8 fire; no multiple attack penalty

---
**Reset**
The Last Crucible deactivates and resets 10 minutes after it has no target creatures (because the creatures either left area H4 or died). Any thoqquas that still live sense the magma river at area H6 and eventually make their way north to that area to swim away.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 203 **Complexity** Complex The lingering essence of the dwarven worshippers who established this shrine demand deference to Torag and punish those who don't offer it. --- **Stealth** DC 27 (expert) to hear whispered prayers in Dwarven to Troag **Disable** Diplomacy DC 27 (trained) to calm the lingering essence, Religion DC 23 (expert) to perform the required obeisance, or Thievery DC 30 (expert) to disrupt and redirect the essence harmlessly. **Prostrate** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)); Trigger A creature moves more than 10 feet into the room. Effect A great weight settles on all creatures in area A4, and they must attempt a DC 25 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected by the haunt and is temporarily immune to it for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature feels pressed down by the weight— it takes a 10-foot penalty to all its speeds for as long as it remains in the room.
**Failure** The creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).
**Critical Failure** The creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) for 1 round. --- **Routine** (3 actions; [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) Ghostly images of chanting dwarves float through the room, drifting between the creatures in the chamber. As they float, they use their 3 actions to target up to three different creatures in the room, touching their brows and filling that person's head with overwhelming but entirely mental choirs exalting the glory of Torag. The haunt targets [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) creatures before other creatures, and a single creature cannot be targeted more than once per round. A targeted creature must attempt a DC 25 Will save; prone creatures take a –2 penalty on this saving throw.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 1d10 mental damage from the cacophonous choir in their head.
**Failure** The creature takes 2d10+9 mental damage from the cacophonous choir in their head.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 3d10+18 mental damage from the cacophonous choir in their head and is knocked prone. --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates as soon as no living creatures are in area A4, then resets after 1 hour has passed. It can be permanently destroyed by clearing the fortress of all creatures that don't follow Torag and rededicating it to the god with a [consecrate](/Rituals.aspx?ID=8) ritual.

**Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 47 **Complexity** Complex The stink of bile suddenly grows as the myriad mouths carved into the walls begin to vomit forth a deluge of acidic slurry. --- **Stealth** +28 (master) **Disable** DC 33 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to disrupt the trap's magical network of sensors and effectively “blind” it to targets to react to, DC 38 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) to recognize the carvings and recall one of the mantras needed to pass safely, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (7th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 32) to counteract the trap. **Vomit** **Trigger** The trap's sensors notice a creature on the stairs north of the entrance to area D4; **Effect** The myriad mouths on the walls spew out a foul-smelling acidic slurry along the entire stairwell. The stairs in areas D3 become difficult terrain, and all creatures in area D3 must attempt a DC 34 Reflex saving throw. A creature that is [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) by hunger takes a –2 circumstance penalty to this saving throw. The trap then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 4d6 acid damage and is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34).
**Failure** The creature takes 8d6 acid damage, is sickened 2, and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 16d6 acid damage, is sickened 3, is knocked prone, and then tumbles down the stairs. The fall ends once the creature reaches the next lowest landing (note that a creature falling at the lowest flight tumbles into the carrion pit at area D2, but can attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) as detailed in that room). A creature that falls down the steps takes an additional 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) from the tumble, regardless of the total distance traveled. --- **Routine** (1 action) On its turn, the trap Vomits as its action. As long as the Putrid Rise is active, the stairs in area D3 are difficult terrain. --- **Reset** The trap deactivates 1 round after no targets can be sensed, but resets immediately.

**Source** [The Haunted Shore](/Sources.aspx?ID=358) pg. 25 **Complexity** Complex Fires suddenly spring up along the rafters of the exposed roof as strange, monstrous shapes can be glimpsed in the sky above, which is suddenly filled with smoke. --- **Stealth** +13 (expert) **Disable** DC 26 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) (trained) to extinguish fires swiftly or DC 23 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (expert) to exorcise the haunt; two total successes are required to disable the haunt **The Sky Breathes Smoke** **Trigger** A living creature ends their turn inside the schoolroom; **Effect** Harrowing shrieks and frightening howls echo from the skies above as smoke plumes down into the rooms below. All creatures in the schoolhouse (areas **A4a–A4c**) must attempt a DC 21 Fortitude save to avoid becoming [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 from the smoke (sickened 2 on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (4 actions) Ghostly figures flying in the skies above hurl bits of burning debris down into the three rooms of the schoolhouse below. The haunt uses its first three actions to target a random creature within the schoolhouse with a burning debris ranged Strike. A creature can’t be targeted more than once per round—if there aren’t enough targets for all 3 Strikes, the leftover Strike actions are wasted. On its fourth action, the haunt causes the fires in the building itself to flare up— all creatures inside the building take 2d8 fire damage (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). These flare-ups are the most extreme in area **A4a**; creatures in areas **A4b** or **A4c** gain a +2 circumstance bonus on this Reflex save.
**Ranged** [one-action] burning debris +15, **Damage** 1d6 bludgeoning plus 1d6 fire --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates and then resets after 1 round in which no living creatures are within the schoolhouse.

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 63 **Complexity** Complex A shaft of light shines from the ceiling to the floor in a ring of slowly churning smoke. --- **Stealth** +33 (master) **Disable** DC 43 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to use tools to reflect and focus the light shining from above into the surrounding smoke to disperse it and the hazard’s magical energies, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial **A Quick Death** ([incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696)) **Trigger** A living creature steps into the central 15-foot area of the room directly illuminated by light; **Effect** The triggering creature momentarily becomes convinced they have been dead for a long time, and that the events of this adventure are but a hallucination. If the triggering creature has come close to death earlier in this adventure, they briefly believe that they didn’t actually survive that encounter. The creature must attempt a DC 38 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature shakes off the conviction that they are dead and realizes it was a magically induced hallucination. The Trial of the Gods deactivates.
**Success** The creature becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), and the conviction that they are dead and now watching, as a ghost, their companions from the middle of the room. The Trial of the Gods rolls initiative, and the creature remains paralyzed until the end of the hazard's next turn.
**Failure** As success, but the creature becomes [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) until the end of the trial's next turn instead of paralyzed. While unconscious, the creature experiences a dreamlike vision of being carried through the River of Souls toward the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39), where their soul shall be judged.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature becomes [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), or increases the value of an existing doomed condition by 1. If the creature dies as a result of this, the Trial of the Gods deactivates. --- **Routine** (1 or 2 actions; [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1524), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) If a creature in area **B4** is paralyzed or unconscious as a result of A Quick Death, the trial’s first action is to Sustain that paralysis or unconscious effect; the paralyzed or unconscious creature can attempt a new DC 38 Will save at this time against this effect with the same potential results as detailed above for A Quick Death, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such save. The Trial of the Gods’ second action is to manifest horrifying ghostly shapes in the smoke that shriek and telepathically threaten everyone in area B4, promising them their deaths are imminent. All creatures other than the paralyzed or unconscious creature currently enduring A Quick Death must attempt a DC 38 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** The creature becomes frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature becomes frightened 3 and is [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) as long as they remain frightened. --- **Reset** Once the room is empty of living creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 8" pfs="">[The Watching Lords](/Hazards.aspx?ID=447)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 104

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The demigod statues in the alcoves seem to shift, their heads turning to watch as intruders pass by.

---

**Stealth**
DC 28 (trained)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) DC 31 (to scrape away hidden runes that grant the statues the ability to watch), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) DC 28 (to pray for protection from the attention of Abyssal lords), or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (4th level; counteract DC 26) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the trap

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Conjure the Guardians** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33)) **Trigger** A non-chaotic-evil creature approaches within 20 feet of the doors to area **G4**; **Effect** The statues appear to hiss and growl, and a moment later, four [brimorak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2896) demons appear in the hallway—two near the entrance to area **G1**, and two near the entrance to area **G4**. The four demons attack at once, rolling initiative as normal. They fight to the death, but vanish after 1 minute has passed.

---
**Reset**
Once the Watching Lords are triggered, the trap needs an hour to recharge its energies, after which point it can be triggered again.

**Source** [The Cellars](/Sources.aspx?ID=360) pg. 72 **Complexity** Simple When the bin is opened, it collapses, spilling out the infested corpse within. --- **Stealth** DC 27 (expert) **Disable** DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (expert) to reinforce the bin so it doesn’t collapse (although if the PCs then search the remains, they still trigger the hazard), DC 27 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to exorcise the haunt. **Horrific Infestation** (curse, fear, mental, occult) **Trigger** The seed bin is opened, or the body within is jostled or searched; **Effect** The body spills out and splits open, releasing an agonizing scream. All creatures in area **C4** must succeed at a DC 29 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 and [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) as long as they remain frightened on a critical failure). The ghoulish gardeners in area **C7** come to investigate soon thereafter. The creature who triggered the haunt must also succeed at a DC 29 Will save with the following effects as it takes a blast of spore-like seeds to the face. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected by the infestation.
**Success** The creature believes it inhaled some of the stuff, and becomes [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 2.
**Failure** As success, but the creature now fears that it’s infected by the corrupt seeds, and imagines it can feel plants growing inside itself. This is all in the creature’s mind, but for the next 8 hours, the sensation makes it [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 2.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the clumsy condition has an unlimited duration.

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 36

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

Nearly imperceptible runes set off an explosion at the point a thief is most unable to receive aid.

---

**Stealth**
DC 50 (master) to notice that the hairline cracks on the passage walls actually form runes.

**Disable**
DC 45 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (10th level, [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 50) to counteract the runes

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Explosion** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature crosses a rune; **Effect** The runes unleash a gout of fire roaring up the chute. Anyone in the chute and within 5 feet of its openings is dealt 8d10+44 fire damage (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Immediately thereafter, the runes emanate a 4th-level [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287) effect for 1 minute, so anyone injured in the chute can't call out for help.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets in 1 minute.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 8" pfs="">[Thin Ice](/Hazards.aspx?ID=690)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=591" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Wight Queen's Thaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=314) pg. 129

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

The white-and-blue ice is less structurally sound than it looks.

---

**Stealth**
DC 28 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 31 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) (expert) to spread out and prevent the ice from cracking further, or DC 31 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (trained) to get off the ice safely as it cracks.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Crack** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** Two or more creatures step onto the ice in area M8; **Effect** The ice beneath the party cracks. All creatures in area M8 must attempt a DC 30 Reflex save. On a failure, they fall into the freezing water, whereupon they must succeed at a basic DC 30 Fortitude save against 4d10+22 cold damage. On a critical failure, the creature must start holding their breath or risk [drowning](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439) as their muscles lock and they begin to sink. A creature must spend an action to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) to the shore and must then succeed at a DC 30 Athletics check to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) up out of the water.

---
**Reset**
The river freezes over every night, restoring this hazard. The hazard disappears once the vernal equinox passes.

All creatures in area A must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude save. On a failure, the target is dazzled and deafened until the end of its next turn (or blinded and deafened on a critical failure). The hazard then rolls initiative. Routine (1 action; visual) The Thin Wisps continue to launch fireworks until the dottari excruciator divisions are defeated. Each round, all creatures must succeed at a DC 24 Fortitude save or be dazzled and deafened for 1 round (or blinded and deafened for 1 round on a critical failure).

<title level="1" right="Hazard 4" pfs="">[Titanic Flytrap](/Hazards.aspx?ID=37)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 78

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

On the surface, a titanic flytrap appears to be a patch of the more common flytrap plant, but beneath murky waters it hides a far larger set of jaws, reaching 10 feet across and reinforced with woody branches and lined with paralytic hairs.

---

**Stealth**
DC 25 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 22 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (trained) to mislead the flytrap’s sense of weight and pressure

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 21, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +8

**HP**
56 (BT 28)

**Immunities**
mental

**Resistances**
acid 20, fire 10

</column>

**Snap Shut** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A Small or Medium creature moves into a square that is within reach of the flytrap’s hidden jaws; **Effect** The flytrap’s jaws snap shut, making a jaws Strike against the triggering creature.

 **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> jaws +17, **Effect** devour 

**Devour** The target is trapped by the flytrap’s jaws, gaining the [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) condition until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 21). Additionally, it is exposed to the titanic flytrap toxin from the hundreds of tiny hairs that line the inside of its leaves. If the flytrap’s jaws Strike was a critical success, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its saving throws against this poison. At the end of each of target’s turns that it remains grabbed, the target takes 3d6 acid damage.

 **Titanic Flytrap Toxin** ([contact](/Traits.aspx?ID=37), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 21 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 4 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d6 poison damage and [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d6 poison damage and stunned 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d6 poison damage and [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) (1 round)

---
**Reset**
1 hour (or longer, after a large meal)

<title level="1" right="Hazard 2" pfs="">[Toppling Furniture](/Hazards.aspx?ID=139)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 65

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A mischievous spirit pushes a bookshelf over onto a creature.

---

**Stealth**
DC 18 (trained) to hear the spirit's grunt of exertion as it works to topple the furniture

**Disable**
DC 16 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) to hold the furniture upright or DC 18 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to foil the spirit's efforts to influence matter

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Topple Furniture** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature moves adjacent to the furniture; **Effect** The spirit shoves the furniture over in an attempt to crush the triggering creature. The triggering creature takes 2d10+7 bludgeoning damage (DC 22 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). On a failure, the creature is additionally knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

---
**Reset**
If the haunt successfully damages a creature with Topple Furniture, the spirit laughs for 1d4 rounds as the haunt resets; each subsequent time the haunt activates, it must topple a different piece of upright furniture. If the haunt fails to damage a creature, the spirit wails in frustration and resets after pouting for 1d4 hours.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 4" pfs="">[Toppling Shelves](/Hazards.aspx?ID=364)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #188: They Watched the Stars](/Sources.aspx?ID=194) pg. 58

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

This stone bookshelf is badly compromised. It's just one push away from toppling over.

---

**Stealth**
DC 18 (trained) to notice the shelf's precarious instability

**Disable**
DC 22 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (expert) or [Engineering Lore](/Armor.aspx?ID=22) (trained) to shore up the shelf

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 18, **Fort** +8, **Ref** +8

**Hardness**
8

**HP**
30 (BT 15), any attack that fails to destroy the shelf triggers its Topple reaction

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Topple** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The shelf is attacked or touched forcefully (such as by a creature [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) into it); **Effect** The shelf tumbles over in the direction opposite its triggering creature, crashing onto the ground in a 10-foot-by-10-foot area. Creatures in the area take 4d8+10 bludgeoning damage (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). A creature that critically fails its save falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The affected area becomes difficult terrain.

 If the toppling shelf crashes into a space occupied by another toppling shelf, it triggers that shelf's Topple reaction. This can result in a chain reaction that causes multiple shelves to Topple, one after the other.

fields.disable: Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the flames. Water typically clears a 5-foot square if the amount is small (such as that from  create water  or  hydraulic push ). <column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #145: Hellknight Hill](/Sources.aspx?ID=4) pg. 9

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A fire engulfs the western door and a 10-foot-by-10-foot area immediately east of it, then spreads on each of its turns.

---

**Stealth**
–10; initiative modifier is +5

**Disable**
Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the flames. Water typically clears a 5-foot square if the amount is small (such as that from [_create water_](/Spells.aspx?ID=53) or [_hydraulic push_](/Spells.aspx?ID=154)). Larger amounts of water, such as a full bucket, typically douse a 10-foot-by-10-foot area (or 4 squares in some other shape). Throwing a bucket of water on flames requires an Interact action. A [waterskin](/Equipment.aspx?ID=62) doesn't contain enough water to put out even 1 square of fire. [Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) can also put out fire, but only if the cold can affect an area; cold is usually less effective than water, so a [frost vial](/Equipment.aspx?ID=77) typically puts out 1 square of fire, and [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245) is ineffective.

 Fountain Circle, located outside town hall, has several working water pumps. These are far enough away that it's impractical for a PC to bring water back and forth. However, a PC might instruct the more steely nerved spectators to create a bucket brigade. It takes 15 spectators (which can include those rescued by councilors as well as by PCs) to set this up, and 2 rounds for the townspeople to line up and begin pumping water from Fountain Circle. As of the 3rd round, there is a bucket of water available for the PCs to use at the chamber's southern entrance at the beginning of each PC's turn. Members of a bucket brigade are lined up outside the chamber, and don't take damage from smoke inhalation.

 If a PC does want to carry the water, it's 150 feet from the chamber's southern door to a pump, so it 6 actions are usually needed to reach the pumps or return. Filling a bucket requires an Interact action.

 Other methods might also help control the fire, as you determine. For example, the PCs might be able to find something to barricade the fire with to control its path, or use a cloak to beat out some of the fire.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---
**Routine**
On its turn, the fire spreads into a number of additional squares equal to half the number of squares the fire currently occupies, with a minimum of 1 square. You determine the squares the fire spreads into—typically those with the most flammable materials. Any creature that ends its turn next to the flames takes 1d6 fire damage, and any creature within the flames takes 4d6 fire damage. Both of these have a DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. A creature can take damage from flames only once per round. (For simplicity, track damage only for the NPCs and their allies, not for the spectators; Turn 5 and Turn 7 have instructions regarding the spectators' health).

 The fire has an additional effect on each of its turns after the first.

 **Turn 2** The chamber's northern door flies open and flames burst through, igniting the 10-foot-by-10-foot area in front of the door. All fires spread on subsequent turns, at the same rate listed above. Any fires that join together become one fire for this purpose.

 **Turn 4+** Creatures in the room take 1d6 damage from smoke inhalation at the ends of their turns. Anyone who uses an Interact action to tie a wet rag around their nose and mouth (or uses another creative solution) halves the damage.

 **Turn 5** Spectators still inside the room fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) from burns and smoke inhalation.

 **Turn 7** Spectators still in the room die.

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 84

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The smoking furnace begins to hiss and click, and its vents swivel and adjust to spew toxic fumes in the direction of intruders.

---

**Stealth**
+15 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 25 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to render one of the vents useless, or DC 25 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) to wrench and bend a vent until it no longer functions

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 24, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +11

**Vent Hardness**
10

**Vent HP**
18 (BT 9); **Furnace Hardness** 15, **Furnace HP** 56 (BT 28)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Spew Toxins** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A visible living creature enters the room, or a Stealthy creature fails to remain [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from the toxic furnace with a DC 25 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check (the trap's sensors have [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) and [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21)); **Effect** One of the toxic furnace's vents swivels to aim at the triggering creature and then spews a gout of boiling toxin at the target. The toxic furnace then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The trap loses 1 action for each disabled vent. On each of the trap's actions, a vent spews a gout of boiling toxin at a living creature in sight of it. It can't target a single creature more than once per round, so if there aren't enough viable targets for all 3 actions, the trap loses those unspent actions.

 **Ranged** boiling toxin +17 ([range 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 1d6 acid, 2d6 fire, and 2d6 poison

---
**Reset**
The trap resets after 1 minute, during which it sees no creatures to target.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [The Towers](/Sources.aspx?ID=366) pg. 218 **Complexity** Complex A ghostly image of one of the Arudoras floats in the middle of the room, arms folded over their chest as if reclining in a coffin, yet they hover vertically and are shrouded by ribbons of green smoke. --- **Stealth** +31 (master) to notice that the eerie manifestation is dangerous; noticing the ghostly image of the Arudora in question floating in the middle of the room has a DC of 0 **Disable** DC 41 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to exorcise the haunt, or one of the following checks depending on the Arudora; four total successes are required to disable the haunt. **J3a (Jinnivere)** DC 38 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) to draw upon her love of horses
**J3b (Dazerien)** DC 38 [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) to frighten the cruel murderer
**J3c (Ryhasphinea)** DC 38 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to trick her into believing she’s been forsaken by Urgathoa
**J3d (Augsten)** DC 38 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to explain that abuse of the servants shows weakness of character
**J3e (Alisendra)** DC 38 [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) to give her one last entertainment
**J3f (Raudltz)** DC 38 [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) to help him come to terms with the shame he feels for his infidelities
**J3g (Irrokcis)** DC 38 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) to use his own obscure theories against him to banish him **AC** 36, **Fort** +28, **Ref** +22, **Will** +30 **Hardness** 22 **HP** 90 (BT 45) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Weaknesses** vitality 15 **Awaken** (emotion, fear, mental, occult) **Trigger** A living creature ends their turn in the room; **Effect** The soul’s eyes open, and it cries out in agony as its ghostly body twists and transforms into something monstrous. The triggering PC must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2 (frightened 3 and [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) for as long as they’re frightened on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) On its initiative, the haunt transforms into a physical manifestation of that Arudora’s personality and lashes out, dealing 9d6 damage to all creatures in the room and within 30 feet of any open doorway outside the room. A PC can attempt a DC 34 basic saving throw against the damage. The type of damage and saving throw to defend against it depend on the Arudora, as does the additional condition imparted on a critical failure. Conditions imparted by this haunt are curses that have unlimited durations.
**J3a (Jinnivere)** trampling horses (bludgeoning damage, Reflex save, [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 on a critical failure)
**J3b (Dazerien)** complex torture devices (piercing damage, Reflex save, [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 on a critical failure)
**J3c (Ryhasphinea)** skull-faced spirits (spirit damage, Will save, [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 on a critical failure)
**J3d (Augsten)** barbed whip and scourge Strikes (slashing damage, Reflex save, enfeebled 1 on a critical failure)
**J3e (Alisendra)** shrieking spirits and discordant instruments (sonic damage, Fortitude save, stupefied 1 on a critical failure)
**J3f (Raudltz)** ghostly fangs that chew into your thoughts (mental damage, Will save, [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 on a critical failure)
**J3g (Irrokcis)** decaying skeletal limbs (void damage, Fortitude save, drained 1 on a critical failure) --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates as soon as no living creatures are in the room, then immediately resets.

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 54

**Complexity** Simple

An oversized cauldron rigged as an elevator suddenly drops 30 feet if it's overloaded.

---

DC 18 (expert)

[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 18 (trained) to lock the releasing mechanisms in place, or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) DC 20 to rig additional supports for the cauldron (this activity requires 10 minutes of work)

**Release the Cauldron** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** More than one Medium or more than two Small creatures are inside the cauldron when it is activated to lower; **Effect** The cauldron releases from its anchor points on the chains and drops 30 feet to area E1; any creatures within take 15 points of bludgeoning damage in the fall. A creature can attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) to avoid falling by clinging to a chain.

---

Stealth DC 18 (expert) Disable Thievery DC 18 (trained) to lock the releasing mechanisms in place, or Crafting DC 20 to rig additional supports for the cauldron (this activity requires 10 minutes of work) Release the Cauldron Reaction Trigger More than one Medium or more than two Small creatures are inside the cauldron when it is activated to lower; Effect The cauldron releases from its anchor points on the chains and drops 30 feet to area E1; any creatures within take 15 points of bludgeoning damage in the fall. <title level="1" right="Hazard 1" pfs="">[Trapped Gate](/Hazards.aspx?ID=532)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #213: Thirst for Blood](/Sources.aspx?ID=257) pg. 33

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A hair trigger rings an alarm and launches a small assortment of wooden spikes to impale anyone attempting to open the gate incorrectly.

---

**Stealth**
DC 17 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 15 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to disable the thin trigger that snaps when attempting to open the gate.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 16, **Fort** +10, **Ref** +2

**Hardness**
5

**HP**
20 (BT 10)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2190), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

</column>

**Impale Trespasser** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature attempts to open the gate; **Effect** A loud alarm rings and set of wooden spikes swings up from below and over the gate, dealing 3d8 piercing damage to the triggering creature (DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). If the creature takes damage from the spikes, they also become [Grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the gate. The creature can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 17). If the creature succeeded at their basic Reflex save, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their checks to Escape, as the spikes didn’t fully impale them. If the creature critically failed their basic Reflex save, they take a –2 circumstance penalty to their checks to Escape, as the spikes are embedded particularly deep.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 10" pfs="">[Trapped Lathe](/Hazards.aspx?ID=72)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 7

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The powered lathe's springs have been critically overwound so that when jostled or triggered, the lathe unwinds violently, hurling blades, gears, and sharp shards of metal around the room.

---

**Stealth**
+19 (expert); DC 29 to notice the line of cord running from the lathe's trigger toward the door to area A2.

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 31 (expert) on the lathe releases the tension on its springs without unleashing its blades and gears.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 30, **Fort** +22, **Ref** +14

**Hardness**
18

**HP**
72 (BT36)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Unleash Fragments** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The lathe is jostled or damaged, or its trigger is remotely pulled. **Effect** The trap makes a sharpened fragment Strike against a random target in area A1, then rolls for initiative.

---
**Routine**
(4 actions) The lathe attempts four sharpened fragment attacks against creatures in the room, selecting a target randomly from all available targets in area A1. The trap does not take multiple attack penalties for any of its attacks. The trap loses 1 action each turn as its springs wind down, and becomes disabled when it has 0 actions.

 **Ranged** <actions string="Single Action" /> sharpened fragment +26, Damage 2d8+12 slashing plus 1d8 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) on a critical hit

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 387 **Complexity** Simple Two portcullises drop down to block progress through this area. --- **Stealth** D 36 (master) **Disable** DC 33 (master) to disable the trigger that causes the portcullises to drop **AC** 30, **Fort** +24, **Ref** +18 **Portcullis Hardness** 18 **Portcullis HP** 72 (BT 36) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Drop from Ceiling** **Trigger** A character enters a square between the two portcullises; **Effect** Both portcullises drop from the ceiling; attempting to lift one requires a DC 30 Athletics check to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34). When the portcullises drop, creatures in adjacent squares must attempt a DC 30 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The creature is unharmed and can take a [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=87) as a reaction to move to an adjacent square.
**Success** As critical success, but the creature takes a glancing blow from the falling portcullis for 2d12+15 bludgeoning damage.
**Failure** The creature is struck by the falling portcullis for 4d12+30 bludgeoning damage and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) in their square.
**Critical Failure** The creature is struck by the falling portcullis for 6d12+45 bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) by the portcullis as it pins them to the ground until they can [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the portcullis (DC 30). --- **Reset** The trap can be manually reset with a 10-minute Manipulate activity performed in the hallways to the east or west of this area, as long as neither portcullis is broken or destroyed.

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 77 **Complexity** Simple The footing on this sloped ground appears to be stable at first glance, but the tiny rocks that cover it are loosely packed and prone to slipping. --- **Stealth** DC 23 (trained) **Disable** DC 20 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (trained) to navigate a safe path **Rockslide** **Trigger** A creature steps on the unstable ground; **Effect** Rocks tumble and slip beneath its feet. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 21 Reflex save as they tumble against the rocks, which deal 2d10+13 bludgeoning damage. **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) in its space.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage, falls prone in its space, and tumbles down to the bottom of the slope.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but double damage.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 10" pfs="">[Tree of Dreadful Dreams](/Hazards.aspx?ID=73)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 11

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The statue of the willow tree animates, its branches lashing out to try to grab anyone in area B2.

---

**Stealth**
+22 (expert)

**Disable**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 25 (trained) to force or lever open a single branch, disabling that branch and freeing any creature trapped within. Thievery DC 29 (expert) to disrupt the tree's magical animation, shut it down, and free all trapped creatures. Placing a [_dreamstone_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=507) in the tree's trunk takes 2 Interact actions and causes the trap to shut down, freeing all trapped creatures. Placing the _cursed dreamstone_ from area B4 in the trunk instead increases the tree's actions per turn to 4 and gives it a +2 item bonus to all saving throws and attack rolls.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 30, **Fort** +22, **Ref** +14

**Branch Hardness**
10

**Branch HP**
40 (BT 20) to break each branch

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Attack of Opportunity** <actions string="Reaction" /> The tree of dreadful dreams can attempt up to six [Attacks of Opportunity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=3) each round.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The statue uses each action to attempt a branch Strike against a random creature in the room that it hasn't grabbed. If there are no creatures for it to attack and it has at least one creature grabbed, it instead Constricts. The trap can have up to six creatures grabbed.

 **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> branch +26 (reach 20 feet), **Damage** 2d10+12 bludgeoning plus the target is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the tree; no multiple attack penalty

 **[Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=10)** <actions string="Single Action" />; 1d10+12 bludgeoning, DC 27

 **Terrifying Visions** A creature that begins its turn grabbed by the trap experiences vivid, warped visions of true events and must succeed at a DC 31 Will save or take 4d8 mental damage. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9). A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates and resets if it has no creatures grabbed and no creatures in the room to attack. If an uncursed _dreamstone_ is placed in its trunk, the statue doesn't reactivate.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 5" pfs="">[Trial By Flame Trap](/Hazards.aspx?ID=711)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=646" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Disgraced Dollmaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=331) pg. 66

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

Nozzles connected to reservoirs of alchemist’s fire are hidden just under the packed dirt of the floor, ready to spew burning jets when deployed.

---

**Stealth**
DC 26 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to disable the nozzles or DC 26 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (expert) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Burning Jets** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An operator at the maze console in area **A13** pulls the associated lever; **Effect** Three [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) nozzles rise from the ground, and each makes a flame jet Strike against a creature in the area marked on the map. A creature can be hit more than once if there are fewer than three targets. On a critical hit, the target takes 1d10 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). **Ranged** flame jet +17 (alchemical, fire, range 20 feet), **Damage** 3d8+10 fire; no multiple attack penalty

---
**Reset**
The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area **A13** pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 5" pfs="">[Trial By Ice Trap](/Hazards.aspx?ID=712)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=646" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Disgraced Dollmaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=331) pg. 66

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A hidden vent in the ceiling is attached to a reservoir of freezing alchemical reagents that can create a bone-chilling cloud.

---

**Stealth**
DC 26 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to jam the vent closed or DC 26 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (expert) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Frozen Mist** <actions string="Reaction" /> (alchemical, cold) **Trigger** An operator at the maze console in area **A13** pulls the associated lever; **Effect** A vent opens in the ceiling, issuing forth a cloud of frigid fog that quickly fills the area marked on the map. Each creature in the area takes 6d8 cold damage (DC 26 basic Fortitude save). Creatures that fail the save also take 1d8 [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (2d8 persistent cold damage on a critical failure). The area remains cold for the next minute, dealing 2d6 cold damage (DC 22 basic Fortitude save) to any creature who ends their turn in the area.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area **A13** pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 63

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

What appears to be an eye opens within the glowing orb near the ceiling.

---

**Stealth**
+33 (master)

**Disable**
DC 43 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to deactivate the glowing orb and prevent it from observing the room, [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial, DC 45 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to perform a complex 5-round candle- lighting ritual, or placing General Ordulf’s religious symbol on an empty hook on any wall as an Interact action

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 40, **Fort** +32, **Ref** +26

**Glowing Orb Hardness**
28

**HP**
110 (BT 55)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Wrath of the Gods** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature attempts to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) or [Pick the Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412) on the eastern door, or ends a turn in this room while not performing the candle-lighting ritual; **Effect** A glowing red eye manifests in the ceiling mounted orb to stare angrily at the triggering creature, who must succeed at a DC 46 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). The Trial of the Gods then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action; [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) The red eye glances at a randomly determined creature in area **B3** that it can see and is not engaged in a candle-lighting ritual, then casts a 9th-rank [_vision of death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1742) on that target, causing them to experience the sight of Achaekek rising up from the ground to smite the transgressor for failing to honor the gods.

---
**Reset**
Once the room is empty of creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 17" pfs="">[Trial of Tolerance](/Hazards.aspx?ID=456)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 61

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A convincing illusion of a bustling market scene fills the empty room, confronting the viewers with potentially frightening diversity and unexpected encounters.

---

**Stealth**
+33 (master)

**Disable**
DC 43 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to scratch out well-hidden key runes etched into the room’s floor, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Unveil the Bazaar** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature begins its turn in area **B2**; **Effect** A convincing illusion of an Ilizmagorti city bazaar appears, complete with a cloudless blue sky above. The surrounding crowd is dense, and the smells and sights and sounds are quite realistic even as no one in the crowd actually bumps against the PCs as they mill about. The Trial of Tolerance then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action; [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) An unexpectedly aggressive or frightening looking figure, such as a Hellknight, demon, pirate, or cloaked assassin suddenly emerges from the crowd and quickly advances toward a randomly determined character in the room, then stands menacingly in their path until the end of the round before they appear to lose interest and drift back into the crowd. If the target has a type of fear or hatred toward a specific kind of creature, this unexpected figure epitomizes those fears and hatreds. The target must succeed at a DC 46 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (or frightened 2 on a critical failure). If any creature in the room takes any hostile action against the intimidating figure, the Trial of Tolerance uses its Reflective Violence reaction. Once three rounds pass without the Trial of Tolerance using Reflective Violence, the hazard deactivates.

 **Reflective Violence** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature uses a hostile action against an illusory figure created by the Trial of Tolerance or fails at an attempt to disable the trap; Effect The illusory figure effortlessly avoids the triggering action, then appears to attack the triggering creature using its most harrowing and violent option. Regardless of what this attack appears as, the triggering creature takes 3d12+19 mental damage (DC 38 basic Reflex save).

---
**Reset**
Once the room is empty of creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 99 **Complexity** Complex Seldeg’s ritual nears its conclusion, causing magical energy to arc erratically between the ritual circles. --- **Stealth** +25 (master) to notice the buildup of divine energy and anticipate its discharge. **Disable** DC 44 [Arazni Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or Iomedae Lore to recount a tale from history that grounds that deity in the current reality, DC 50 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (legendary) to create a device to siphon energy from the ritual circle, or DC 46 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (legendary) to discharge the escalating divine energy; six successes (three successes per circle) are required to disarm the hazard **Reorder Reality** **Trigger** A creature other than [Seldeg](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3832) enters the area contained by the ritual circles; **Effect** Arcs of divine energy travel between the two circles. Each creature within the circles takes 4d10+26 spirit damage (DC 45 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). If one of the ritual circles has been disabled, the hazard instead affects all creature in the room, but each creature gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their save. The hazard rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action; [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) The divine energy gathered by the ritual spikes. One of the eleven stained-glass windows (each depicting one of her Eleven Acts) transforms to feature [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=326) instead. Any creature that can see the window change must attempt a DC 50 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is immune to this effect for 10 minutes.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature takes 3d12+20 mental damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 6d12+40 mental damage. If the creatures’ next d20 roll is a critical success, they earn a critical failure instead. This is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.
If all 11 windows transform, Seldeg’s ritual finishes ahead of schedule. The stained-glass windows shatter, dealing 8d10+52 piercing damage (DC 50 Reflex save) to each creature in the room. The hazard then becomes inactive. --- **Reset** While atop the floating platform, Seldeg Bhedlis can use a 3-action activity with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait to reenergize the ritual. Doing so removes one success to disable the hazard and immediately triggers the hazard’s Reorder Reality reaction.

fields.disable: DC 32 Nature or Occultism (expert) to perform a ritual to ward the area against  fey intrusion, DC 34 Performance (master) to meet the Twisted King's demands with a disturbing dance, or DC 32 Athletics or Intimidation (expert) to fend off or frighten the fey dancers. Three total successes are required to disable the haunt, and each check takes 2 actions.
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 18 **Complexity** Complex Countless fey with grisly visages and misshapen bodies cavort throughout the room, kicking up caustic debris and pulling other creatures into their dangerous dance. --- **Stealth** +20 (trained) **Disable** DC 32 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) to perform a ritual to ward the area against fey intrusion, DC 34 [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) (master) to meet the Twisted King's demands with a disturbing dance, or DC 32 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (expert) to fend off or frighten the fey dancers. Three total successes are required to disable the haunt, and each check takes 2 actions. **Welcome to the Feywrithe** **Trigger** 1 round passes since both isqulugs in area **B6** are slain, or 10 rounds pass since they rolled initiative; **Effect** The isqulugs die horribly (if they're still alive), rent by clawed fey hands. Spectral fey pull at the other creatures in the caves, all of which must attempt a DC 36 Fortitude save. The haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [pulled](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet toward the standing stones.
**Failure** The creature is pulled 15 feet toward the standing stones.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pulled 15 feet toward the standing stones, knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), and takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage (in addition to any damage from the toxic water). --- **Routine** (1 action) Spectral fey cavort about the room. All creatures in the room are raked by ghostly claws and splashed with toxic water, taking 1d10+14 force damage and 2d10 acid damage (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Creatures that critically fail their Reflex saves are [pulled](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet toward the standing stones. --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates after 1 minute. It re-forms every new moon. If all of the glyphs in area **B6** are restored—a process requiring 10 days of downtime and 10 successful DC 36 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) checks—the haunt becomes permanently disabled and doesn't re-form.
