**Source** [Pathfinder #181: Zombie Feast](/Sources.aspx?ID=139) pg. 42 **Complexity** Complex The former bank manager's ghostly presence tempts creatures to partake in a dubious meal. --- **Stealth** +22 (trained) **Disable** DC 18 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to say a prayer to [Urgathoa](/Deities.aspx?ID=19) and put the haunt temporarily to rest until it resets, DC 22 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to commune with the bank manager's spirit and convince her to permanently pass on, disabling the haunt **Foul Temptation** ([necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** A creature looks over the contents of the desk; **Effect** The haunt tempts nearby creatures to eat from the plates and bowls arrayed on the desk by concealing it in an illusion of food the viewer finds delicious. Each creature in area D5 must attempt a DC 21 Will save. The haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature sees through the illusion entirely and is temporarily immune to the haunt's routine for 1 minute.
**Success** The creature is not tempted by the food.
**Failure** The creature believes the food is appetizing and becomes driven to consume it. The creature takes 4d4+4 slashing damage as it chews the jagged bones and husks.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature takes double damage and is [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) for 1 round as the haunt continues to tempt it. --- **Routine** (1 action) The haunt sends a cloud of dust and bone shards hurtling about the room. The dust and bones batter all creatures in the room, dealing 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Creatures who fail the save are [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). --- **Reset** The haunt re-forms after 1 hour. The haunt becomes disabled and doesn't re-form if a creature eats a full meal at the desk—this can be any food, not just the “food” at hand.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 9" pfs="">[Unbearable Sorrow](/Hazards.aspx?ID=410)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 34

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

The PCs hear the sound of sobbing and feel an overwhelming sense of sorrow, as if they'd lost something more precious to them than their own life.

---

**Stealth**
DC 30 (master)

**Disable**
DC 32 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) (master) to laugh away the sadness, DC 31 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (expert) to banish the psychic imprint, DC 33 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to disperse the emotional energy

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Mourn** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** A living creature approaches the statue; **Effect** The trap deals 4d10+14 mental damage to all creatures in the room (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). On a failed save, a creature additionally falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and begins to weep, taking 1d10 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

---
**Reset**
The trap resets automatically after 24 hours.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 26 **Complexity** Complex A sphere of concentrated agony harvested from a [qlippoth](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=146) begins pulsing with violet light as it blasts the room with otherworldly agony. --- **Stealth** +27 (master) **Disable** DC 37 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to dismantle the housing and refocus the agony inward so it consumes itself harmlessly, DC 33 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (master) to vent the agony in a controlled way that causes the _portalrender_ to become inert after 1 minute (during which it can still be triggered normally), or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (7th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 31) **AC** 34, **Fort** +26, **Ref** +20 **Hardness** 22 **HP** 88 (BT 44) **Agonizing Pulse** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** The unfinished _portalrender_ takes any damage or is moved (the _portalrender_ is Bulk 5); **Effect** The central sphere of concentrated agony flashes bright violet, filling the mind's of the room's inhabitants with overwhelming mental sensations of pain and hallucinations that the world around them is being torn away and replaced by a demon-haunted apocalypse. All creatures in area B4 must attempt a DC 33 Will save, then the trap rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 4d6 mental damage from the pain.
**Failure** The creature takes 8d6 mental damage from the pain and is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) until the end of their next turn.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 16d6 mental damage from the pain, is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37), and is confused for 1 minute. --- **Routine** (1 action) The unfinished _portalrender_ continues to flood area B4 with agony, and everyone in the room must attempt a DC 33 Will save against its Agonizing Pulse. At the end of its turn, the unfinished _portalrender_ attempts a DC 6 flat check. On a failure, its stores of agony deplete and it deactivates, causing the central orb of agony to fade away permanently

fields.text: Hazard 13 Unfinished Portalrender Complex Magical Trap Source Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger pg. 26 Complexity Complex A sphere of concentrated agony harvested from a qlippoth begins pulsing with violet light as it blasts the room with otherworldly agony. Stealth +27 (master) Disable DC 37 Thievery (master) to dismantle the housing and refocus the agony inward so it consumes itself harmlessly, DC 33 Arcana or Occultism (master) to vent the agony in a controlled way that causes the portalrender to become inert after 1 minute (during which it can still be triggered normally), or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 31) AC 34, Fort +26, Ref +20 Hardness 22 HP 88 (BT 44) Agonizing Pulse Reaction (emotion, enchantment, mental, occult) Trigger The unfinished portalrender takes any damage or is moved (the portalrender is Bulk 5); Effect The central sphere of concentrated agony flashes bright violet, filling the mind's of the room's inhabitants with overwhelming mental sensations of pain and hallucinations that the world around them is being torn away and replaced by a demon-haunted apocalypse. All creatures in area B4 must attempt a DC 33 Will save, then the trap rolls initiative. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature takes 4d6 mental damage from the pain. Failure The creature takes 8d6 mental damage from the pain and is confused until the end of their next turn. Critical Failure The creature takes 16d6 mental damage from the pain, is stupefied 1, and is confused for 1 minute. Routine (1 action) The unfinished portalrender continues to flood area B4 with agony, and everyone in the room must attempt a DC 33 Will save against its Agonizing Pulse. At the end of its turn, the unfinished portalrender attempts a DC 6 flat check. On a failure, its stores of agony deplete and it deactivates, causing the central orb of agony to fade away permanently

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 79 **Complexity** Simple A trail of over-sized footprints crosses the path, markings of the apparently recent passage of a dangerous and mind-shattering entity whose stride is enough to be mistaken for depressions in the natural terrain, and promising destruction to those compelled to follow the tracks. --- **Stealth** DC 46 (master) **Disable** DC 46 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) (master) to distract those (including yourself) compelled to follow footprints, or DC 43 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) (legendary) to quickly obscure the trail **Beckoning Trail** (mental); **Trigger** A creature crosses over the footprints’ trail; **Effect** The triggering creature suddenly realizes the nature of the immense trail they just stepped into and feels a compulsion to follow the trail to their destination; the triggering creature must attempt a DC 35 Will save with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature Strides once down the trail before coming to their senses—this movement does not put the creature in any peril or danger.
**Success** The creature takes its three actions to Stride down the trail. While this movement doesn’t put the creature in any direct peril, when they end the movement, they’re overwhelmed with the knowledge that had they gone further, something horrible would have happened; the creature becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 hour by the close call.
**Failure** As success, but the creature becomes [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 and also stupefied 1 for 24 hours.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but doomed 2 and stupefied 2. In addition, at the end of the three Strides, the creature vanishes from view, instantly teleporting to some dangerous area or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) prison. This might be a nearby location that the creature’s allies can discover and rescue them from, or it may be somewhere further away that will require more effort to reach before the victim can be rescued. --- **Reset** The unspeakable impressions fade once they are triggered, but reform somewhere else in the vicinity 24 hours later unless they are successfully disabled.

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />

**Source** [Pathfinder #186: Ghost King's Rage](/Sources.aspx?ID=189) pg. 50

</column>

The _Fiendflame Cage_ is uncontrolled, releasing holy light and hellfire in the area.

---

**Stealth**
+48 (legendary)

**Disable**
DC 48 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) four times on the _Fiendflame Cage_ to calm it through ritual incantations

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 9 **Complexity** Complex An unsettling wave of malice and sinister energy ripples invisibly out from the manor, causing those who view the building to see a leering, evil face glaring at them from the structure’s architecture. --- **Stealth** DC 32 (master) **Disable** DC 32 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to exorcise the haunt, DC 35 [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) to approach the manor in a proper way that defers to its occupant's symbolic standing in the community; displaying an official pass that legally grants permission to enter the building reduces both of these DCs by 5 (provided the PCs approach the front door and not from another direction). **Horrifying Vision** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1524), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** A Small or larger creature approaches within 30 feet of the house's exterior; **Effect** A wave of malice fills the minds of all living creatures outside of the manor within 60 feet with overwhelming fear; each creature must attempt a DC 29 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Horrifying Vision for 24 hours. In addition to this temporary immunity, the creature can attempt a DC 23 Occultism or Religion check as a free action to notice that despite there being only one face in the facade, several spiritual echoes seem to infuse the building. On a critical success, the creature realizes that only the most powerful force infusing the manor is evil and that the other elements are non-hostile spirits who are overwhelmed and trapped by that singular force.
**Success** The creature experiences a brief vision of the manor's facade twisting into an immense, horrific face and becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1. The creature can attempt the same Occultism or Religion check as above, but the DC increases to 33.
**Failure** As failure, but the creature becomes frightened 2 and is [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) for as long as it remains frightened. The creature can attempt the Occultism or Religion check to Recall Knowledge normally (DC 33).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature can't reduce its frightened condition below 1 for 1 minute. In addition, the overwhelming fear causes the creature to become [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1; this condition persists until it's cured magically or the hazard is disabled. --- **Reset** The unwelcoming facade resets immediately if not disabled and can be triggered again the very next round.

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane ](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 15 **Complexity** Complex The spirits of the island’s citizens manifest and panic as the vault fills with seawater. --- **Stealth** +22 (expert) to sense the terror of the spirits inside the vault **Disable** DC 33 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (trained) twice to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) the vault’s door or DC 30 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (trained) three times to exorcise the spirits **Flooding Vault** **Trigger** A living creature spends more than 1 minute inside the vault; **Effect** The vault’s door slams shut, trapping any creatures inside. Meanwhile, the souls of the dozens of citizens who died when Pakilykos sank manifest throughout the vault. The haunt then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) Water begins to fill the vault from a crack in the floor hidden beneath the bones. The spirits of the citizens panic and grasp at the living, begging them to act. Each creature in the vault takes 2d10+13 void damage with a basic DC 28 Fortitude saving throw. On a failure, the creature is also [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 (or enfeebled 2 on a critical failure).
The first time the hazard takes this action, water fills the vault to knee-height, making the area difficult terrain. The second time the hazard takes this action, the vault fills halfway with water, and creatures inside must succeed at a DC 15 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check each round to Swim. The third time the hazard takes this action, the vault fills entirely with water, and creatures inside must hold their breath. --- **Reset** The waters recede and the spirits disappear once no living creatures remain inside the vault, but the haunt resets immediately, triggering again if a living creature steps inside.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 9" pfs="">[Velicarn's Head](/Hazards.aspx?ID=768)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=622" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Private Halls](/Sources.aspx?ID=363) pg. 166

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A hideous mound of flesh, shattered bone, tangles of hair, and what appears to be gray matter lies in a glistening, 2-foot-tall heap on the floor, only to suddenly start piling up on itself to gradually form an immense, hateful head.

---

**Stealth**
+23 (master) to notice the mound of gore is haunted; noticing the mound itself has a DC of 0

**Disable**
DC 30 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (expert) to exorcise the haunt; three successes area required to disable it

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 31, **Fort** +21, **Ref** +15

**Hardness**
18

**HP**
70 (BT 35)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

**Weaknesses**
vitality 10

</column>

**Awakened Horror** <actions string="Reaction" /> (auditory, emotion, fear, mental) **Trigger** A living non-fiend creature approaches within 15 feet of the remains of Velicarn’s head; **Effect** The mound of gore shudders and quakes, then starts to pile up on itself, slowly transforming into an immense, screaming head. All living creatures in area **F1** must attempt a DC 28 Will save as the gurgling birth-shriek of the awakening horror tears through the room. Those who fail become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its turn, Velicarn’s head continues to grow and expand as it becomes a monstrous distortion of his once-human appearance, with beady red eyes, sharp fangs, and two bat-like wings that unfurl from either side. The haunt screeches louder, and all creatures in the library take 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) as blood pours from their ears, eyes, and mouths (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). If Velicarn’s head isn’t disabled or destroyed by the end of the third round, it rips out of the ground and joins the fight as a horrific monstrosity—a daqqanoenyent. At this point, the haunt is automatically disabled, and the PCs must face this new threat. As a daqqanoenyent, Velicarn’s head focuses its attacks on the PCs and ignores the sahkil (who, if still alive, titters and cackles in delight at this development). It pursues PCs relentlessly and fights until it’s destroyed, which permanently destroys the hazard.

---
**Reset**
Velicarn’s head collapses back into a 2-foot-high mound of gore at the end of any round in which no non-fiend living creatures are in the library. It then resets 1 minute later.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 18" pfs="">[Venom Pool](/Hazards.aspx?ID=126)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 11

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A shallow, foul-smelling puddle of toxic acid blocks a narrow hall, and poison bursts from it when disturbed.

---

**Stealth**
+30 (legendary) to distinguish between the hazard and the oozes within it; DC 0 to notice the pool

**Disable**
DC 40 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) (master) or DC 42 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (legendary) to neutralize the acid while within reach of it. Three successes using either skill (or a combination of both) destroys the hazard.

**Deadly Footing** The area of the venom pool is difficult terrain, and each creature moving through it takes 10 acid damage for every square of its area that it moves into.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Poison Puff** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature moves through any square in the hazard's space; **Effect** The pool produces a 9th-level [_cloudkill_](/Spells.aspx?ID=42) (DC 40) at its center. It then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) The hazard uses its first action to spread 10 feet down the hallway in both directions. Once out of the hall, each side spreads in a random direction each round, but they don't go through doors. The hazard uses its second action to move the center of the _cloudkill_ up to 20 feet in any direction to which any part of the pool has line of effect (normally, to encompass the greatest number of characters). If the _cloudkill_ isn't present, it instead uses its second action to produce a new cloudkill, as Poison Puff.

---
**Reset**
The hazard ends after 1 minute, contracting to its original size and keeping still until disturbed again.

With their reach and ability to manifest from any part of the machinery, these Strikes can target any creature in the room. They only target a creature more than once if there’s not enough targets to split their attention.

Stealth DC 23 (trained) to feel an ominous presence in the room Disable DC 19 Occultism (trained) to disperse the force or DC 20 Religion (trained) to ward yourself from harm Shove Reaction Trigger A creature moves adjacent to the haunted wall; Effect A powerful force sweeps across the room, shoving all creatures in the room toward the wall. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature is pushed 5 feet toward the wall. If the creature would collide with the wall, they take 1d10+5 bludgeoning damage. Failure The creature is pushed 10 feet toward the wall. If the creature would collide with the wall, they take 2d10+10 bludgeoning damage. Critical Failure The creature is pushed 15 feet toward the wall. If the creature would collide with the wall, they take 3d10+15 bludgeoning damage and are knocked prone. Reset 1 day

fields.disable: DC 50 Thievery (master) to disrupt the rune projecting Asmodeus’s face or DC 48 Religion (master) to refute the Asmodean faith; four total successes are required to disable the hazard
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Midnight Burning](/Sources.aspx?ID=346) pg. 187 **Complexity** Complex A looming illusory image of the face of Asmodeus appears within the room, eyes glinting with malice at any who refuse to worship him. --- **Stealth** +35 (master) to find the face-projecting rune **Disable** DC 50 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to disrupt the rune projecting Asmodeus’s face or DC 48 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to refute the Asmodean faith; four total successes are required to disable the hazard **Menacing Laughter** (auditory, emotion, fear, mental) **Trigger** A creature who doesn’t worship Asmodeus enters the room; **Effect** The booming voice of Asmodeus laughs cruelly at nonbelievers who would dare enter his highest temple on Golarion. Each creature who doesn’t worship Asmodeus within 100 feet must attempt a DC 48 Will save. The hazard then rolls initiative as Asmodeus’ face appears in the middle of the vestry. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2.
**Failure** The creature is frightened 3 and [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for as long as they’re frightened.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but frightened 4. --- **Routine** (1 action; mental, visual) The illusory face of Asmodeus gazes at one creature in the area who doesn’t worship Asmodeus. His eyes glint with diabolic power as that creature is overwhelmed by visions of the enormity of Hell. That creature must attempt a DC 44 Will saving throw. The hazard tends to target creatures who are attempting to disable the hazard. Taking damage from this hazard doesn’t grant a flat check to end the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) condition. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 5d8 mental damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 10d8 mental damage and is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 20d8 mental damage and is confused for 1 minute. --- **Reset** The trap deactivates 1 round after all creatures who don’t worship Asmodeus either leave the room or are dead. It resets 1 round after that.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 8" pfs="">[Vision of Dahak](/Hazards.aspx?ID=66)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #146: Cult of Cinders](/Sources.aspx?ID=7) pg. 10

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Blasts of fire and smoke pour out of the tunnel walls to coalesce into the burning form of [Dahak](/Deities.aspx?ID=150) himself; a PC who succeeds at a DC 20 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) notes that the fiery dragon closely resembles classical depictions of the draconic god of destruction.

---

**Stealth**
+16 (expert)

**Disable**
[Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) DC 26 (expert) to utter prayers to a nonevil deity to counteract Dahak's presence (prayers to [Apsu](/Deities.aspx?ID=149) allow this check to be made if the character is merely trained in Religion), [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 30 (expert) to divert the hazard's energies back upon themselves, or a successful [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (4th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 26).

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 27, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +13

**HP**
130

**Immunities**
critical hits, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), object immunities, precision damage

**Weaknesses**
[cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 10

</column>

**Manifest** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature is within the way station. **Effect** The vision of Dahak appears in a 15-foot space adjacent to that creature and rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) The vision of Dahak manifests next to the creature that is closest to the center of the way station, then uses its Breath Weapon in a direction that catches the most possible targets in its area.

 **Breath Weapon** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=13)) The vision of Dahak unleashes a blast of fire from its burning maw, creating a 60-foot cone that deals 6d6 fire damage to all creatures within (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

---
**Reset**
The vision of Dahak deactivates and resets automatically once no creatures remain within the Huntergate way station.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 61 **Complexity** Simple An ornate wooden throne decorated with the Eye of Aroden offers a harrowing and very realistic vision to those who sit upon it. --- **Stealth** DC 22 (trained) **Disable** DC 22 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to deface [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) runes that trigger the trap or DC 24 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to blunt the trap’s magical effects. Once disabled in any of these ways, the vision of netherspace still grants the complex vision, but the triggering creature ignores the effects of a failure or critical failure, treating both of those instead as successes. **Impart Vision** ([mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature sits on the throne; **Effect** The creature experiences a brief but complex vision over the course of a round that appears to the creature to take quite a bit longer. In the vision, the triggering creature suddenly sees monstrous, shadowy figures flitting about the ship’s deck—mechanical men, amorphous blobs, reptilian giants, and so on. The figures move at irregular, inconsistent speeds and intersect one another at times, as if the viewer is watching a series of recorded images taken over decades interposed atop one another and replayed all at once.

In their mind, the sitter hears several whispering voices speaking to them at once in a dozen different languages. Many sound human, but others sound like the turning of cranks, the sibilance of a swarm of snakes, the buzzing of insects, and stranger. Anyone capable of speaking even a single language can make out the gist of what the voices are saying—“take me home,” “release us from our prison,” and so on. A particularly loud voice calls out: “Seize the _cubic helm_. Release the ship. Let yourself go, and we will show you how.” The triggering creature must attempt a DC 21 Will save at this time. **Critical Success** The creature gains exact knowledge of how an ether ship and its components (including the cubic helm, ether sails, and phase spike) function.
**Success** The creature gains exact knowledge of how a cubic helm functions.
**Failure** The creature’s perception of the vision feels as if it persists for hours; they emerge from the vision with a headache but no insights into the function of the ship or its components. The PC takes 2d8 mental damage.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the vision feels like the passage of days, not hours. The creature takes 4d8 mental damage and becomes [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73).

<title level="1" right="Hazard 13" pfs="">[Wailing Crystals](/Hazards.aspx?ID=77)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 9

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Three clusters of gleaming, colorful crystals are corrupted with necromantic energy that causes them to reflect negative emotions. All three must be disabled or destroyed to negate the hazard.

---

**Stealth**
+27 (master) or DC 37 (master) to notice what appear to be screaming ghostly faces in the crystals

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 29 (master) to carefully fracture the crystals or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) DC 27 (expert) to place objects to stop the resonance, both disabling one 5-foot patch of crystals.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 34, **Fort** +26, **Ref** +18

**Hardness**
18

**HP**
72 (BT 36) per 5-foot patch

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Echoing Cry** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)); **Trigger** A living creature approaches within 20 feet of a wailing crystal. **Effect** A despairing chorus of cries echoes off the crystals, working its way into the minds of all living creatures in Jewelgate Way Station, affecting them with [_crushing despair_](/Spells.aspx?ID=57) (7th level, DC 33). The hazard rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The hazard uses each action for an Anguished Shriek. The wailing crystals lose 1 action for each 5-foot patch of crystals that is broken or destroyed.

 **Anguished Shriek** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) A shrieking, distorted face composed of writhing necromantic energy lances out of the crystals to target a random living creature within 20 feet. The target takes 4d6 mental damage and 4d6 sonic damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).

---
**Reset**
The wailing crystals deactivate and reset once no living creatures are within 20 feet.

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 79 **Complexity** Simple A massive sculpture of a wolflike form as tall as a mountain guards passage to the Cold Wastes at the northern end of Leng and seems almost ready to come to life at the approach of any creatures. --- **Stealth** DC 48 (master) to realize the mountain is dangerous (DC 0 to see the towering statue in the first place) **Disable** DC 51 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) (master) to avoid the initial notice of the gigantic form, or DC 48 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (legendary) to know the proper posture and hand sign to make to turn away the watcher’s attention **Dreadful Notice** (incapacitation, mental, occult, visual); **Trigger** A creature comes within a mile of the mountain-sized statue’s base; **Effect** While the Watcher does not actually animate, it fills the triggering creature’s mind with the dread conviction that it might do so at any moment. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 42 Will save, after which they are temporarily immune to that particular Watcher’s Dreadful Notice for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 24 hours.
**Failure** The creature is stupefied 3 (unlimited duration).
**Critical Failure** The creature is [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) with fear with an unlimited duration; as long as the creature remains paralyzed, they need not drink or eat. If they are brought to a location where they no longer have line of sight to the watcher, the paralyzed creature can attempt a new Will save every day to recover from the paralysis, but during this time they are subject to thirst and starvation as normal. --- **Reset** The nightmare resets immediately.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #163: Ruins of Gauntlight](/Sources.aspx?ID=71) pg. 37 **Complexity** Complex An overwhelming feeling of being watched wells up in the minds of those in the room, an instant before an eerie red eye opens in the western wall. --- **Stealth** +12 (expert) **Disable** DC 22 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) (trained) to appear uninteresting to the watching eye (and thus be ignored by it) or DC 22 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to ward against being seen by or affected by the eye **AC** 21, **Fort** +14, **Ref** +8, **Will** +8 **Hardness** 12 **HP** 50 (BT 25) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Weaknesses** positive 5 **Someone is Watching** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A living creature remains in area **C4** for at least 1 round; **Effect** An overwhelming wave of paranoia fills area **C4**. Each creature in the room must attempt a DC 25 Will save, with the following results. An eerie red eye then opens in the center of the western wall, looking about the room, and the haunt rolls initiative.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 and feels like someone or something is watching them for as long as they remain frightened.
**Failure** The creature becomes frightened 2 and treats no one as an ally as long as they remain frightened.
**Critical Failure** The creature becomes frightened 3 and is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) as long as they remain frightened. --- **Routine** (1 action) The eye glances about, and those it can see (whether in area **C4** or outside of it) take 4d6 mental damage (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save) as fears of being watched impart ripples of pain. A creature that takes mental damage from this effect doesn’t reduce their frightened value at the end of their next turn. --- **Reset** The haunt becomes inert at the end of any round in which there are no frightened creatures it can see. It stays dormant for 1 hour, after which point it resets.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Midnight Burning](/Sources.aspx?ID=346) pg. 181 **Complexity** Complex A torrent of souls pulled from Hell pours through an archway, inflicting their personal suffering on all they touch. --- **Stealth** +43 (master) **Disable** DC 50 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (master) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to quell the souls’ suffering; these checks must be attempted while adjacent to the arch, and four total successes are required to disable the haunt **Rising Tide of Screams** (auditory, divine, emotion, fear, mental) **Trigger** A living creature comes within 15 feet of the arch; **Effect** The sounds of screams from the damned intensify as the arch begins to glow with planar energy. Each living creature within 60 feet of the arch must attempt a DC 48 Will saving throw. The haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2.
**Failure** The creature is frightened 3 and can’t reduce its frightened condition below 1 for the haunt’s duration.
**Critical Failure** The creature is frightened 4 and can’t reduce its frightened condition below 2 for the duration of the haunt. --- **Routine** (1 action; divine, void) A seemingly endless flow of damned spirits emerges from the arch and washes down the street. Each creature within a 240-foot line from the arch down the street takes 4d10+24 void damage with a DC 44 Fortitude save. This line affects everyone within 20 feet of the ground. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and increases its [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) value by 1.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and increases its doomed value by 2. --- **Reset** After 1 minute, the wave of souls dries up, and the haunt deactivates. Over the course of 1 hour, planar energy rebuilds in the area, and the haunt resets.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 11" pfs="">[Weakened Floor](/Hazards.aspx?ID=437)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=591" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 11

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The weakened floor gives way with a tremendous crash, dropping everything in the room into a muddy morass of toxic mold.

---

**Stealth**
+23 (master)

**Disable**
DC 33 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (master) three times to knock holes in the floor without triggering the spore cloud while simultaneously lightening the strain on the floor so it can be walked upon, DC 36 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) (expert) to move carefully through the room for the remainder of your turn without triggering the hazard, or DC 36 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) (expert) twice once the trap is triggered to knock enough holes into the nearby walls to cause the spores to disperse.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Collapse Floor** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A round begins with a Small or larger creature standing on the floor in area A4; **Effect** The floor of the entire room collapses in a thunderous crash, dropping all creatures in the room 5 feet into a soupy morass of mud, mold, and toxic fungus while a cloud of spores spews up into the air above. The room becomes greater difficult terrain. All creatures who were standing on the floor in the room fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) in the mess below unless they succeed at a DC 34 Reflex save, in which case they land on their feet. The hazard then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) Every round on its turn, the spores that now fill area A4 inflict 8d6 poison damage to all creatures in the room (DC 30 basic Fortitude save) as the cloud burns at exposed flesh; a creature that holds its breath gains a +4 circumstance bonus to this saving throw.

---
**Reset**
One minute after nothing moves in the room, the spores settle down. The floor remains obvious and won’t collapse further, but any creature that moves through the mold causes the spores to plume up again, re-triggering the trap.

**are**

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 527 **Complexity** Complex An ornate wheel set into a wall—divided into six segments with colored runes on each—is controlled by a magical sensor that detects any creature within 100 feet in front of it. --- **Stealth** +16 (expert) to detect the magical sensor; noticing the wheel has a DC of 0 **Disable** [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 26 (expert) on the wheel to stop it from spinning, Thievery DC 22 (master) to erase each rune, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (4th level; counteract DC 22) to counteract each rune **AC** 24, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +13 **Hardness** 14 **HP** 56 (BT 28) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Wheel Spin** **Trigger** A creature enters the sensor’s detection area. **Effect** The wheel begins to spin and rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (2 actions) On its initiative, the trap uses its first action to spin, then stops. Roll 1d6 to determine which segment is topmost when the wheel stops spinning. The wheel uses its second action to replicate the spell listed for that segment (3rd level, DC 24, spell attack roll +14). This spell’s target is centered on or otherwise includes the nearest creature in the area. This increases the spell’s range to 100 feet if necessary. Any spell cast by this trap is arcane.
  1. [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=288)

  3. [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172) (100-foot line)
  4. [_blindness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=26)
  5. [_acid arrow_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2)
  6. [_ray of enfeeblement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=244)
--- **Reset** The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any creature moving within range of its sensor.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 7" pfs="">[Whispers From Long Ago](/Hazards.aspx?ID=443)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 75

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

As the door is opened, unsettling whispering radiates outward, worming its way into the mind of the one who dared intrude.

---

**Stealth**
DC 27 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 27 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to deface the subtly hidden triggering runes around the door's circumference, or _dispel magic_ (4th level; counteract DC 23) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the trap

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Protect the Stone** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature attempts to open the door or damages the door with a Strike or spell; **Effect** The door whispers into the triggering creature's ear, speaking in one of the following three languages: Shoanti, Thassilonian, or Varisian. If the target creature speaks any of these languages, it hears the whispers in the tongue it is most comfortable speaking. If the target does not speak these languages, the trap's whispers have no effect. If the target understands the whispers, the trap casts [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1693) on the target (DC 25 Will save), suggesting they “stand guard before the door and fight any who attempt to pass by it to enter the chamber beyond until Mistress Liralarue's arrival.” Once, the whispers also alerted Liralarue, but as she is long gone now, the PCs don't need to fear the arrival of a powerful runelord's apprentice.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets over the course of a round and is ready to whisper at the next person who attempts to open the door 1 round later.

Each creature in the line must attempt a DC 29 Reflex save. Moving above ground against the direction of the line is [greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for 1 minute. **Critical Success** The creature is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet along the line.
**Success** The creature takes 5d6 bludgeoning damage and is pushed 15 along the line.
**Failure** The creatures takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed 30 feet along the line, and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 20d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed 45 feet along the line, is knocked prone, and is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) for 1 round.If the line overlaps a body of water, the winds cause massive waves that deal 6d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in the water or within 15 feet of the waterline (DC 29 basic Reflex save). On a critical failure, a creature is also swept 30 feet away from the waterline and 15 feet beneath the water's surface.

Failure The creatures takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed 30 feet along the line, and is knocked prone. Critical Failure The creature takes 20d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed 45 feet along the line, is knocked prone, and is stunned 1 for 1 round.If the line overlaps a body of water, the winds cause massive waves that deal 6d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in the water or within 15 feet of the waterline (DC 29 basic Reflex save). On a critical failure, a creature is also swept 30 feet away from the waterline and 15 feet beneath the water's surface.

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 43 **Complexity** Simple Necromantic magic stored in runes painted in powdered bone and banshees’ tears lash out at anyone other than Heh Shan-Bao who opens the secondary compartment. --- **Stealth** DC 37 (master) **Disable** DC 37 [Disable Device](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to scratch out the runes and dissipate their magic harmlessly, DC 40 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) to sabotage the spell and cause the runes to dry up and blow away as inert powder, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (7th level; counteract DC 31) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the runes **Withering Wail** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** Someone other than Heh Shan-Bao opens the secondary compartment; **Effect** A howling, spectral face manifests out of the chest and screeches, causing all within area C4 to attempt a DC 33 Fortitude save; the sound also alerts the jiang-shi in areas C3a and C6, who quickly come to investigate the sound. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 7d6 negative damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 15d6 negative damage. In addition, their flesh withers and weakens, leaving them to appear old and decrepit—the creature becomes [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 and [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 until the curse is removed.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 30d6 negative damage and becomes cursed as failure, but becomes clumsy 2 and enfeebled 2.

These heavy doors, carved with an image of [Dahak](/Deities.aspx?ID=150), echo with a hatred so powerful that it can kill anyone who comes nearby, manifesting a vision of Dahak's head emerging from the doors to strike at a foe.

**Stealth**
+22 (expert) to notice subtle vapors of magical energy seething across the doors

[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 29 (expert) to disrupt the divine magic, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) DC 29 (expert) to placate the wrathful energies, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (5th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 26).

18

72 (BT 36)

**Immunities**
critical hits, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Expunge** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A non-worshipper of Dahak touches either door leading to C7; **Effect** The hazard targets the creature with Face of the Fatal Divine, then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its initiative, the wrath of the destroyer targets the closest target in area C6 with Face of the Fatal Divine.

 **Face of the Fatal Divine** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The creature beholds the face of Dahak as it emerges to bite with its burning jaws, targeting the creature with [_phantasmal killer_](/Spells.aspx?ID=219) (5th level, Will DC 29).

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any creature being in range

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 47 **Complexity** Complex Narseigus's worm-calling enchantments have attained imperfect control over Zogototaru, compelling her to aid him. She follows his directions loosely and with little finesse. --- **Stealth** +15 **Disable** DC 28 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or DC 28 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to identify a loophole in mind-controlling magic, DC 30 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to reason with Zogototaru, or DC 31 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) to speak as if the PC were Taargick --- **Routine** (1 action) Zogototaru acts on Narseigus's most recent command, either Rescuing, Roaring, or Thrashing.
**Rescue** ([move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) Zogototaru lunges near Narseigus, flips him atop her head, and recoils. This moves Narseigus up to 30 feet horizontally and positions him atop Zogototaru, treating her head as a 10-by-10-foot space that's 20 feet above the magma's surface. This movement triggers reactions based on the move trait, targeting Narseigus. Zogototaru continues supporting Narseigus until ordered to perform a different action, after which she deposits him in a safe location within 30 feet as a free action. A PC can [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) (DC 25 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)) Zogototaru's coarse hide to reach him.
**Roar** ([fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) Zogototaru looms and screeches ferociously. Creatures in a 60-foot cone take 6d6 sonic damage (DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) and must attempt a DC 29 Will save. **Critical Success** No effect. **Success** The creature is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19). **Failure** The creature is frightened 2. **Critical Failure** The creature is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1d6 rounds and is frightened 3.
**Thrash** ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) Zogototaru lashes her body, rattling the ground and splashing magma in a 30-foot cone. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 29 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** No effect. **Success** The creature takes 4d6 fire damage. **Failure** The creature takes 4d6 fire damage and 4d6 bludgeoning damage, and is [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 round. **Critical Failure** The creature takes 6d6 fire damage and 6d6 bludgeoning damage, and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). **Special** The first time she Thrashes, Zogototaru destroys the pillars in area **F2a**. Anyone there can leap free as part of their Reflex saving throw, landing on the closest surface. For the remainder of combat, the rear half of the crimson worm's body floats in the magma there, creating an improvised bridge 10 feet wide and 30 feet long. Creatures on Zogototaru take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Reflex saves against her Thrashing.

fields.disable: DC 45 Occultism (legendary) or Religion (legendary) to exorcise Zutha’s spirit, or DC 48 Intimidation (master) or Performance (master) to recite the details of Zutha’s defeat; six total successes are required to disable the haunt.
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 15 **Complexity** Complex The scowling visage of Runelord Zutha appears above the altar. Meanwhile, mask-like versions of Zutha’s face manifest on nearby rubble and vomit swarms of maggots. Once the masks are destroyed, the air fills with spectral duplicates of Zutha’s life-draining bone scythe. --- **Stealth** +48 (expert) to sense Zutha’s hungry spirit before it manifests **Disable** DC 45 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (legendary) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (legendary) to exorcise Zutha’s spirit, or DC 48 [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (master) or [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) (master) to recite the details of Zutha’s defeat; six total successes are required to disable the haunt. **AC** 45, **Fort** +36, **Ref** +27, **Will** +33 **Mask Hardness** 30 **Mask HP** 120 (BT 60); **Scythe HP** 120 (BT 60) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Weaknesses** bludgeoning 20 **Resistances** all damage 5 (except force, _ghost touch_, spirit, or vitality; double resistance vs. non-magical) **Howl of Rage** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=1524), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A living creature attempts to descend the stairwell at area **A1a** into the islet's interior; **Effect** A ghostly version of Zutha's face appears above the island. Meanwhile, the rubble on the islet warps into smaller versions of Zutha's face. The faces howl in rage as one. All creatures on the islet must succeed at a DC 42 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (or frightened 3 on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (4 actions) The haunt uses Vomit Maggot three times, then Poisonous Belch once. For each success at Disabling the haunt, the haunt loses one Vomit Maggot action. Destroying a mask also removes one of the haunt''s Vomit Maggot actions. Once the haunt can no longer use Vomit Maggot, it immediately regains three actions and replaces Vomit Maggot with Spectral Scythe. Destroying a scythe also removes one of the haunt''s Spectral Scythe actions. Once the haunt loses all three of its Spectral Scythe actions, the haunt is destroyed.
  • **Vomit Maggot** One of Zutha''s rubble-masks vomits a swarm of maggots. (The masks appear everywhere on the islet, and destroyed masks reform moments later, making nowhere on the islet safe.) The maggots burrow into the flesh of a creature of the GM''s choice. The creature takes 2d12 [persistent piercing damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save) and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for as long as they continue taking this damage. When the persistent damage ends, the maggots dissolve into foul-smelling oil.
  • **Spectral Scythe** [one-action] (void) One of Zutha''s scythes swipes at a creature of the GM''s choice. The creature must attempt a DC 42 Reflex save with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
    **Success** The creature takes 3d10+10 void damage.
    **Failure** The creature takes 6d10+10 void damage and is [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1.
    **Critical Failure** The creature takes 12d10+10 void damage and is drained 2.
  • **Poisonous Belch** [one-action] (poison) The ghostly image of Zutha''s face belches a toxic cloud that reeks of decaying flesh. The cloud fills a 10-foot burst centered anywhere on the island and lasts until the haunt''s next turn. Any creature that enters the area or that starts its turn in the area must attempt a DC 44 Fortitude save with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
    **Success** The creature takes 5d8 poison damage.
    **Failure** The creature takes 10d8 poison damage and is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1.
    **Critical Failure** The creature takes 20d8 poison damage, is sickened 2, and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for as long as it remains sickened.
--- **Reset** The haunt deactivates once no living creatures remain nearby. The haunt resets 1 hour later.
